terms.gloss: hide something, keep it secret; keep someone in the dark about it
terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation: with two accusatives, cēlāre aliquem aliquid
evidence: Plaut. Bacch. 375–376: ut cēlem patrem … tua flāgitia
Cic. Fam. 2.16.3: nōn tē cēlāvī sermōnem T. Ampiī (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: keep hidden, keep out of sight
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 277: quod cēlātum atque occultātum est ūsque adhūc

terms.gloss: thrust away out of sight, stash away
evidence: Cic. Att. 12.15: māne mē in silvam abstrūsī dēnsam (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: put away, hide; sē abdere, hide oneself
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.126: eās contēxit atque abdidit (nātūra) (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: put carefully out of sight, hide away
evidence: Plaut. Merc. 360: nēquīquam abdidī, abscondidī, abstrūsam habēbam
Cic. Rosc. Am. 41: quō studiōsius ab istīs opprimitur et absconditur (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: nunc hoc mihi factū est optumum, ut tēd auferam, aula, in Fideī fānum: ibi abstrūdam probē
phrases.english: the best thing I can do now, pot, is to carry you off to the shrine of Faith: I’ll hide you well away there

phrases.latin: quod cēlātum atque occultātum est ūsque adhūc, nunc nōn potest
phrases.english: what has been kept secret and hidden until now can be hidden no longer
in vain I hid her, put her away, kept her tucked out of sight

sources: Lewis & Short: celo · Lewis & Short: occulto · Lewis & Short: abstrudo · Lewis & Short: abdo · Lewis & Short: abscondo
